title: `cum_sum` of doubles: one running `+=` in row order, in memory, streaming and per partition under `over`
verdict: the value at row i is the values up to i added one at a time from 0.0, in row order; NULL rows skipped
description: `cum_sum` of a `Float64` column folds `det_sum` over the rows in order: one `f64` state, starting at 0.0 (`init.unwrap_or(T::Native::zero())`), and `*state += v` for each non-NULL value, whose row gets the new state; a NULL row gets NULL and leaves the state as it is (`v?`). There is no compensation and no reordering: the value at row `i` is the sequential sum of the values up to `i`, a sum in the `SEQUENTIAL` order.

On the streaming engine `cum_sum` is a `CumAggNode`: it receives the morsels serially, in order, runs the same kernel on each with the last non-NULL output of the previous one as its initial state (`cum_sum_with_init`), so the whole column is the one sequential fold.

Under `over(partition)` on the streaming engine, the `window` node gathers each partition's rows in input order (a stable counting sort on the partition id, `maintain_order: ordered_eval`) and evaluates the expression on each partition's contiguous slice, so each partition gets its own sequential fold from 0.0.

sverify's translation reads `cum_sum().over(partition)` of a frame's values (NULLs as 0.0, which adds nothing) at the frame's last row when the frame starts at the partition's first row (polars-window-agg): the frame's values added in frame order from 0.0, the sum `WinFn.valueIn`'s sequential reading gives.
reference: A window `SUM` of doubles is a sum of the frame's values in an order the profile's `sum_order` allows (`WinFn.AllowedP`); the sequential order is one of Polars's (`SEQUENTIAL`), so the value is in `Allowed` (`window_sum_algo = RUNNING_ADD`, a sum of exactly the frame's rows).

evidence.note: `cum_scan_numeric`: one state, the rows in order (reversed only for `reverse=True`)
`CumAggNode`: serial receive, `cum_sum_with_init` with the previous morsel's last non-NULL value as the state
`evaluate_partition`: stable counting sort on the partition id, rows in input order (`ordered_eval`), the expression evaluated on each partition's slice
test_native_windows_match_the_row_by_row_oracle: running double sums equal the former row-by-row loop's sequential sums

provenance.notes: `cum_sum` of `[1e16] + [1.0] * 1000 + [-1e16]`: last value 0.0 with `collect(engine='in-memory')`, `collect(engine='streaming')` under `POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=4` (about 250 morsels), and `cum_sum().over('g')` with one partition, streaming. A sequential sum gives 0.0; a tree or a compensated sum gives 1000.0. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.
